title: On‑Call Coverage Strategy and Communication Playbook
author: Leila O'Connor
body:
Overview:

This document describes Redwood's standardized approach to on-call coverage planning, incident runbook usage, post-incident communication, and operational readiness exercises (game days). It consolidates guidance used by SRE, Platform, Serving Runtime, and Customer Success to ensure predictable coverage, clear escalation, and timely customer notifications.

Goals and principles:
- Ensure measurable, continuous coverage for customer-facing SLOs with no single-point-of-knowledge.
- Prioritize fast detection and safe mitigation (stop-the-bleed) while preserving correctness.
- Make communications predictable: internal status updates every 15/30/60 minutes, external updates aligned to severity.
- Keep runbooks actionable, short, and testable in game days.
- Optimize rotations to balance fatigue, knowledge distribution, and on-call capacity.

1) Coverage strategy and ownership matrix

High-level guidance:
- Two-layer model: Tier 1 (primary first responder) and Tier 2 (escalation/triage). Tier 3 is engineering subject-matter experts (SMEs) for long remediation.
- Each customer-impacting service must have a primary and secondary on-call assigned in the coverage calendar. Primary handles initial triage; secondary acts as backup and cross-check.
- Coverage windows default to 8-hour daytime shifts (2 people/day overlap at handoff) and a single overnight on-call for critical systems (rotating weekly).

Example coverage matrix (weekday snapshot):

Service | Primary team | Secondary | Pager threshold | Canonical runbook
---------------------------------------------
embedding-service | serving-runtime | eng-platform | P99 latency > 750ms for 5m | runbooks/embedding-service-latency
auth-gateway | eng-sre | security | 5xx rate > 1% for 10m | runbooks/auth-gateway-5xx
realtime-queue | eng-platform | serving-runtime | consumer lag > 3x baseline | runbooks/realtime-queue-backup

(Teams must append these rows into the central runbook index; use the runbook naming conventions below.)

2) Runbook standards and naming convention

All runbooks MUST include the following top-level sections (in this order):
- Summary (one-paragraph impact/constraints)
- When to run (explicit trigger conditions: metrics and thresholds)
- Safety first (immediate containment steps)
- Triage checklist (diagnostics and quick checks)
- Mitigation (steps to restore service or put safe fallback)
- Rollback / undo steps (how to revert temporary fixes)
- Postmortem pointers (links to the template and required artifacts)
- Ownership and contacts (primary, secondary, pager IDs, runbook owner)

Naming: runbooks/{service-name}/{short-purpose}. Example: runbooks/auth-gateway/fatal-5xx.json. Use lowercase, hyphen delimiting, and include team tag in header metadata.

3) Incident lifecycle and playbook (quick reference)

Severity classification (operational):
- Sev0 (Outage): Multi-region blackout or > 80% customer impact.
- Sev1 (Critical degradation): Major SLO breach for a high % of traffic (P95/P99).
- Sev2 (Partial degradation): Isolated customer impact or partial feature loss.
- Sev3 (Informational): Non-urgent issues with monitoring alerts but minimal customer impact.

Triage flow (numbered steps):
1. Detection: alert fires or customer ticket escalates; on-call acknowledges within 5 minutes for Sev0/Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2.
2. Declaration: primary documents severity, declares incident channel (Slack or incident bridge), and sets initial timeline.
3. Safety: perform "stop-the-bleed" actions per runbook (rate-limit, circuit-breaker, route traffic away).
4. Diagnose: collect traces, logs, metrics, KV cache state, model variants in use, and recent deploys. Use standardized commands:
   - curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/query?service=<svc>&range=5m
   - kubectl -n <ns> get pods -o wide --selector=service=<svc>
   - rtrqctl inspect-lag --service <svc> --window 10m
5. Escalate: if unresolved after 30 minutes for Sev1, page Tier 2 and contact the on-call engineering lead. For cross-team incidents, inform Customer Success within 45 minutes.
6. Mitigate: implement tested mitigation from runbook; if no runbook, follow safe rollback pattern (scale down, revert last deploy, enable degraded mode).
7. Stabilize and handoff: once errors drop below threshold for 15 minutes, create a bridge for follow-up and assign a remediation owner.
8. Resolve and close: finalize chronology, incident ticket, assets (logs, captures, runbook edits), and file a postmortem within 72 hours.

4) Escalation and contacts (communication channels)

Primary channels:
- Internal incident channel: #inc-<service>-<YYYYMMDD> (Slack)
- Incident bridge: +1-XXX-555-0110 (pin-based access)
- Pager: PagerDuty (use urgent for Sev1/Sev0)
- Status page: status.redwood.ai (public updates)

Escalation matrix (contact order for Sev1):
1. Primary on-call (pager)
2. Secondary on-call (Slack DM and pager)
3. Team lead (phone)
4. Cross-team SRE rotation lead (pager)
5. CTO or acting exec-on-call (for multi-service outages)

5) Rotation policy and scheduling algorithm

Design goals: equitable load, multi-experience pairing (junior+senior), predictable handoffs.
Policy highlights:
- Weekly primary rotations for overnight coverage; daily/8h shifts for daytime on-call where teams require higher granularity.
- No engineer takes more than 2 weekend primary shifts in a quarter.
- Mandatory 48-hour cool-down after a Sev1 (no primary shift; may take secondary).
- Buddy handoff: written notes in the incident channel and a 10-minute synchronous check at the start of a new shift.

Scheduling algorithm (runner notes for on-call coordinator):
- Input: team members, blackout dates, skill tags, preferred weeks.
- Hard constraints: vacation blocks (exclusive), maximum consecutive weeks (2).
- Soft constraints: preferred weeks, proximity to release windows.
- Output: publish calendar CSV and sync to PagerDuty with explicit primary/secondary tags.

6) Game day (readiness exercise) playbook

Purpose: exercise runbooks, verify on-call flows, validate customer comm cadence, and surface knowledge gaps.
Cadence and roles:
- Quarterly cross-team game days; focused monthly drills per team.
- Roles: exercise lead (designs scenario), controller (observes timeline), primary responder (responds), secondary support, and postmortem facilitator.

Sample scenario: "Model KV cache corruption at 90% traffic"
- Inject alert: sudden P99 token latency spike and increase in transient memory errors.
- Objectives: runbook execution, estimate RTO under mitigation, confirm status page templates, and practice cross-team triage.
- Post-exercise deliverables: annotated runbook edits, action items assigned, 30-minute hotwash.

7) Status page and customer comms templates

Status page guidance:
- Severity mapping to status page states: Operational (no impact), Degraded Performance, Partial Outage, Major Outage.
- Use plain English, list affected regions/services, provide root cause hypothesis (when known), and include actionable workarounds.
- Avoid internal jargon; include ETA or "We are investigating" when unknown.

Public templates (copy/paste and customize):
- Initial notice (within 15 minutes of customer impact detection):
  Title: "Partial outage affecting <service-name>"
  Body: "We are investigating reports of degraded performance for <service-name> affecting approximately <X%> of requests. Our engineering teams have identified the issue and are actively working on mitigation. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impact: <short list>. Workaround: <if available>."

- Update (example at 60 minutes):
  Title: "Update: mitigation in progress for <service-name>"
  Body: "Engineering has implemented a mitigation that has reduced error rates by <Y%>. We continue to work on a full fix and will update in 60 minutes or sooner. Impact: <current impact summary>. Next steps: <next investigative steps>."

- Resolution notice:
  Title: "Resolved: <service-name>"
  Body: "The incident affecting <service-name> has been resolved as of <time>. Root cause: <summary>. Customer impact window: <start — end>. If you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood.ai with your request id."

Internal customer comms (Customer Success template):
- Short proactive email for high-touch customers:
  Subject: "Service incident affecting <customer-name> — initial notice"
  Body: "Hi <Customer Contact>, we detected a partial outage impacting <feature>. Our SRE and product teams are engaged and we will send targeted updates every 60 minutes. Expected ETA for next update: <time>. We will follow up with a detailed incident report after resolution. — <CS Rep>"

8) Postmortem minimum requirements and timeline

What to submit within 72 hours:
- Incident summary (timeline of detection, mitigation, resolution).
- Root cause analysis with data supporting the claim (logs, trace IDs, config diffs).
- Contributing factors and why prior mitigations did not prevent escalation.
- Severity impact metrics (affected % of requests, users, revenue if applicable).
- Corrective actions with owners and target dates (short-term and long-term).
- Runbook updates and test plan.
- Public-facing postmortem draft for customer comms (if customer-impacting).

Review cadence: postmortems for Sev1/Sev0 reviewed at the monthly reliability review; Sev2 artifacts maintained for trend analysis.

9) Templates and quick snippets (for copy/paste)

Pager acknowledgement snippet:
- "Acknowledged. Investigating (initial triage started). Primary on-call: <name>. Slack channel: #inc-<svc>-<date>."

Runbook header example:
- "Service: auth-gateway
Owner: eng-sre
Primary pager: PD-12345
Last test: 2026-01-12
Doc link: /runbooks/auth-gateway/fatal-5xx"

Postmortem headline example:
- "2026-02-02 — Sev1 — auth-gateway — Root cause: malformed healthcheck rollout caused upstream 502s"

10) Appendix: tooling and observability pointers

Critical helpers:
- Incident tracker: issues.redwood.ai (create incident-<svc>-YYYYMMDD)
- Runbook index: confluence runbooks folder and runbook-linter CLI to validate required fields.
- Automated status updates: status-bot (Slack) integrates with status.redwood.ai for scheduled public updates.

Ownership and enforcement:
- Team leads are responsible for updating runbooks quarterly and running at least one drill per quarter.
- SRE rotation lead monitors on-call load via oncall-analytics and flags burnout patterns monthly.

Related resources:
- /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/slo-policy-2025
- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/service-runbook-index-2025

Questions or suggested edits: ping the SRE rotation lead (Jordan Kim) or file a PR against the runbook index.
